notes.C01: Strong idea for the dub job, but it needs anydub integration, a re-sense per dub and a calibration step before it can act on its own.
notes.C02: Directly fixes the 'read like English' dub pace using signals the tool already has; serves only the dub job.
notes.C03: Targets real, observed ASR failures that poison every downstream job, and keeps errors visible instead of dropping them.
notes.C04: Fits the fact-check job well, and gating it behind --check keeps the default card cost flat; the second backend adds compute.
notes.C05: Works on the most common real input and can remove the heaviest pass (MLX), but the Vietnamese diacritic OCR is untested.
notes.C06: Credit lines are cheap, but the fingerprint morgue and the original-search add a growing store and network calls for a rare job.
notes.C07: Answers the most often repeated real request (link and cite several videos) and saves many tokens; the index needs upkeep.
notes.C08: Big potential token savings, but the rent ledger, leases and crossover knobs are new machinery that needs tuning.
notes.C09: Many harvesters and monthly audits form a standing operational burden on a one-person tool.
notes.C10: Fixes a measured defect (733 dead commands) cheaply and adds an honest degrade ladder; low novelty, high certainty.
notes.C11: Interesting editorial signals, but few of the owner's real jobs need cue sheets or splice forensics.
notes.C12: One roster line serves citing, casting and claim attribution at a small card cost; the name binding needs a judge.
notes.C13: Nearly free to run, but it serves a narrow corner of the dub job.
